subject: lion
reasoning:
I'm planning the lion's proportions and pose, then setting up the skeleton with a root hip joint and a spine chain running from hips through shoulders to the neck and head.

A neck and jaw chain extend to the head, while a separate tail chain curves backward with a tapering radius down to a tufted tip. For the body itself, I'm sweeping a tube along the spine chain with varying radii to shape the rump, belly, and chest, keeping proportions tight enough to leave proper leg clearance underneath.

Adjusting the spine height and radius to get a more believable belly clearance -- lowering the center and shift so the stylized lion body sits around 0.6 to 1.16 in height, then starting to position the front shoulder joints for the legs.

I'm computing front leg segment lengths so a two-bone chain can reach from the shoulder down to a bent foot, settling on lengths that overreach slightly so the elbow bends backward naturally, then setting up the shoulder-elbow-wrist chain for the paw.

For the rear legs, I'm giving each hip joint a three-segment chain—thigh, shin, and metatarsal—bending the knee forward and the hock back so the foot lands near the ground, then naming the joints hipL, kneeL, hockL, and pawHL, making sure the point count matches the expected number of spans plus a tip.

I'm now working out the tapering radii for the sweep geometry of each leg (thicker at the hip, narrowing toward the paw) and adding a flattened sphere for the paw itself, with left/right suffixes applied consistently.

I'm then planning the spine and neck as separate catmull-rom chains: spine points rise gently from the hindquarters toward the shoulders, and the neck branches off the final spine joint to carry the head forward and slightly upward, matching a lion's posture.

For the head itself, I'm using relative local directions off the head joint (forward/up/down/etc.) to place the skull sphere, muzzle frustum box, and jaw, avoiding any world-axis confusion since everything is defined in the head's own local frame.

I'm placing the nose as a small dark box at the top front of the muzzle, then adding amber sphere eyes with black pupils and small brow ridges above them, mirroring left/right using a sign variable. For ears, I'm adding two flattened spheres near the top of the head, with darker inner color, partially hidden by the mane. Now I'm thinking through how to build the mane itself, likely as a ring or scatter of tufts around the neck and head base.

Writing mane geometry...

Placing the tail root just behind the body's rounded rear cap and curving it backward with a catmull spline so it tapers naturally off the hips.

For the hips root joint, I'm thinking the sweep only needs to apply to the spine chain, with the rear cap handled separately since the chain sweep connects through the joints.

The shift value moves the cross-section down along the bone's normal axis since the bone's up vector points vertically when heading forward. I'm shaping the body radius function so it's shallower at the rump and deeper near the chest at t~0.9.

Still working out proportions...

Now I'm adding muscle definition with small bumps for shoulder and haunch, placed as scaled spheres near the front and rear leg joints to give the body some contour under the tan coloring.

I'll let belly countershading handle itself via normals on the tubes, and skip whiskers but add cream-colored whisker pads and chin. I'm skipping claws but adding three tiny cream spheres on the front paws as simple toe details, and leaving the jaw/mouth interior plain for now.

Now I'm positioning the rear paw target and defining a generic limb function that takes a root point, target, segment lengths, and bend directions for each joint—one inner bend for front legs (elbow), two for rear (knee and hock)—with chains parented to the spine or hips. I'm also setting up a sphere helper for eyes and other small parts, and positioning the head joint relative to the end of the neck chain.

I'm adding a jaw joint parented to the head, assigning roles like "spine," "neck," "head," and "tail" to the respective chains, and figuring out where to anchor the mane—attaching it near the neck's second joint so it sits just behind the head. Then I'm scattering mane tufts and chest fur as cones oriented along surface normals, filtering out ones facing too far forward so the mane reads correctly around the head and chest.

Now I'm picking the color palette: dark brown and lighter brown for the mane, tan for the body, cream for highlights, and near-black for the nose. I'm positioning the ears near the top of the mane relative to the head, and working out the symmetric left/right placement for the eyes.
